surface: Zone of facilities outside the well. Power supply, the drive and the arrival of produced fluid are here.
Houses the surface equipment and receives the production that rises through the tubing.
Site electrical energy and produced fluid arriving through the tubing.
Energy toward the drive and fluid toward the production facilities.
Connects the well with the electrical supply and with fluid handling.
power-supply: Surface electrical supply that feeds the ESP system. It does not stand for a specific panel, voltage or grid.
Delivers electrical energy to the drive.
It is the start of the assembly energy path.
vsd: Variable-speed or variable-frequency drive, between the supply and the cable. Its effect on motor speed will be studied later. Frequency is not adjusted or simulated in this stage.
Conditions the electrical energy that will travel down the cable to the downhole motor.
It sits between the surface supply and the cable that goes down the well.
electrical-cable: Power cable that runs down the space between casing and tubing to the motor, at the lower end of the assembly.
Carries electrical energy from the VSD to the motor.
Electrical energy at the downhole motor.
Joins the surface electrical equipment with the motor. It does not feed the pump directly.
well: Conduit between the surface and the zone of interest. The wellhead marks the boundary with surface. Tubing, cable and the ESP assembly are installed inside it. Completion and well pressure are not modeled.
Contains the ESP and gives the fluid a path from the reservoir toward surface.
Housing for the cable, the ESP string and the tubing.
It is the physical setting where the downhole assembly is installed.
tubing: Production pipe hung from the wellhead. It carries fluid from the pump discharge to surface. Friction is not calculated and no diameter is fixed.
Channels the produced fluid toward surface.
Fluid toward the wellhead and the surface.
It continues the fluid path above the pump.
pump: Multistage centrifugal pump, at the top of the downhole assembly. It receives rotation through the shaft and drives fluid into the tubing. There are no curves, efficiency or pumping-energy calculations.
Transfers energy to the fluid so it can be driven toward surface.
Fluid from the intake and mechanical rotation of the shaft.
The motor drives it through the shaft and it discharges into the tubing.
intake: Fluid inlet to the pumping assembly. Well fluid enters here, from the annulus, before the pump. Flow rate is not represented.
Lets well fluid enter the pump.
Connects the inside of the well with the pump. The shaft passes through it.
protector: Seal section between the motor and the intake. It isolates the motor, filled with dielectric fluid, from the well fluid, and lets the shaft pass. Pressures and volumes are not calculated.
Protects the motor from well fluid and passes shaft rotation upward.
Shaft rotation toward the intake and the pump.
Separates the motor from the produced fluid and keeps the shaft mechanically continuous.
shaft: Common shaft of the assembly. It runs through the motor, protector, intake and pump. It represents the mechanical rotation that couples the motor to the pump. Torque, speed and vibration are not modeled.
Transmits motor rotation to the pump.
Mechanically links the motor with the pump through the protector and the intake.
motor: Downhole motor, at the lower end of the ESP assembly. It converts the electrical energy arriving through the cable into shaft rotation. Power, current and speed are not represented.
Turns electrical energy into mechanical energy.
Drives the pump through the ESP assembly shaft.
reservoir: Conceptual origin of the fluid. It shows where the liquid that enters the well comes from. There is no reservoir or productivity model.
Supplies the fluid the ESP will have to lift.
Fluid present in the formation, in a conceptual sense.
Fluid toward the well and, from there, toward the intake.
Starting point of the fluid path.
production-flow: Conceptual path of fluid that has already been lifted, from the pump discharge until it reaches surface. It is not a piece of equipment.
Represents the fluid leaving the well toward the surface facilities.
Closes the fluid path that started in the reservoir.

energy: Electrical energy starts at the surface supply, passes through the VSD and the cable, reaches the motor and becomes shaft rotation that drives the pump. Power and speed are not calculated.
fluid: Fluid leaves the reservoir toward the well, enters through the intake, the pump drives it and it rises through the tubing to surface. Flow rate and pressure are not calculated.
